title: Singing risque lyrics then and now
summary: She says she did not sing things like that in the 1920s, though Susie did, and "Mighty Tight Woman" got many requests in London.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: I know they didn't. They say so many things now they used to wouldn't say. They used to wouldn't say"whiskey"on the air and"damn"to them, (unintelligible) all that kind of stuff, they'd never say nothing like that. No, things sure has been changed, honey. Been changed.
Yeah, but you were singing things in the '20s --
Not like that.
You weren't singing things like that in the '20s?
No.
Well, your friend Susie was singing stuff like that.
Maybe she was, but I wasn't "Shorty George Blues."
Well, when Susie was singing "I bake the best jelly roll in town," what do you think she was singing about?
I didn't know.
You didn't do ______.
No, honey. I wouldn't think say that.
No?
Uh-huh.
When you said, "I'm a mighty tight woman, --"
(Laughter.)
Yeah, but that's ______. Look how long that's been.
Yeah.
That's ______ around the '50s or '40s.
"I'm a Mighty Tight Woman?"
Yeah, I sang "Mighty Tight Woman" in London.
You sang it in 1926 and '29, didn't you?
Yeah, (unintelligible) sang it in London.
"I'm a Mighty Tight Woman?"
Yeah.
I think so.
Yeah, I think I did, too. I think I did, too.
I think so. Well, it's a great song.
Well, I get so many calls for it. They say, "I'm a Mighty Tight Woman," "I'm a Mighty Tight Woman," "I'm a Mighty Tight Woman."
It's such a great song.

They say (unintelligible) say, "What that mean?" I say, "I'm just tight in everything I do." Say, "What do 'mighty tight' mean?" I say, "I'm tight in everything I do." (Unintelligible) kidding now, I'm very tight. They ask me, "Well, what do 'tight' mean?"
